text: Random passenger arrivals and travel-time fluctuations disrupt bus headways, promote bunching, and increase passenger waiting time. Holding control regulates headways by delaying departures, but its effectiveness depends on vehicle states, operating conditions, and the permitted holding duration. text: To address vehicle and stop differences and fluctuating action-value estimates, this thesis constructs a shared holding policy combining categorical embeddings with continuous states and develops Robust Ensemble Soft Actor-Critic (RE-SAC). With the same learner and training settings, learned embeddings reduce generalized passenger time relative to one-hot encoding by 5.51%, 1.41%, and 4.91% under routine operations, demand surges, and rapid switching, respectively. In the multi-line experiment with a headway objective, RE-SAC reduces planned-headway deviation and forward-backward headway imbalance relative to SAC by 5.00 and 7.36 seconds, respectively.
